title: Teaching
text:
Academic coursework, instruction, and mentoring in physics and emerging quantum technologies.
    
  

  
  Courses at IIT (ISM) Dhanbad

  
  
    
      NBEP103
      Monsoon Semester 2026
      Undergraduate Core
    

    Foundation of Physics
    
    
      
      Indian Institute of Technology (Indian School of Mines), Dhanbad
    

    
      A foundational physics course introducing fundamental principles and mathematical formulations across vector calculus, oscillations and waves, general properties of materials, and foudnation of optics. Emphasizes conceptual rigor, analytical problem-solving, and applications to modern science and engineering.
    

    
      
        Course Code
        NBEP103
      
      
        Semester / Term
        Monsoon Semester 2026
      
      
        Instructor
        Dr. Rahul Gupta
      
      
        Institution

  Previous Teaching Experience

  
    
      Uppsala University
      Department of Physics and Astronomy • Sweden
      
        Solid State Physics I: Teaching and problem-solving tutorials.
        Semiconductor Laboratory: Experimental instruction and lab supervision.
        Modern Physics Laboratory: Guided undergraduate and master's students through advanced physical experiments.
      
    

    
      IIT Delhi
      Department of Physics • New Delhi, India
      
        Engineering Physics Laboratory: Teaching assistantship conducting lab sessions, demonstrating optical and electronic setups, and evaluating student laboratory work.
      
    
  

  
  Research Mentoring & Supervision

  
    
      Active mentorship and supervision of postdoctoral fellows, doctoral candidates (Ph.D.), Master's dissertation students (M.Sc./M.Tech), and undergraduate researchers (B.Tech) working on frontier topics in spintronics, orbitronics, terahertz emitters, magnetic heterostructures, and hybrid quantum technologies.

title: News
text:
The latest updates, publications, and announcements from the group.


  
  
  
    
      August 2026  •  Lab Update
    
    
      GHYAN is Established at IIT (ISM) Dhanbad
      
        The Gupta Laboratory for Hybrid Quantum Systems & Spintronics is officially established at the Department of Physics, Indian Institute of Technology (Indian School of Mines) Dhanbad. We are looking forward to building our experimental capabilities and welcoming new researchers to the group.
      
    
  

  
  
    
      February 2025  •  Research Highlight & Press Release
    
    
      Toward Sustainable Computing: Energy-Efficient SOT-MRAM Memory Innovation
      
        A major breakthrough in Spin-Orbit Torque Magnetic Random-Access Memory (SOT-MRAM) led by Dr. Rahul Gupta and collaborators at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (JGU) in partnership with Antaios has been featured internationally. Published in Nature Communications ("Harnessing orbital Hall effect in spin-orbit torque MRAM"), the research demonstrates an over 50% reduction in energy consumption by utilizing orbital currents rather than expensive, heavy metals.
      
      
        
          Federal Ministry of Education and Research in Germany ↗
        
        
          idw News ↗
        
        
          EurekAlert! (AAAS) ↗
        
        
          Quantum Zeitgeist ↗
        
      
    
  

  
  
    
      May 2021  •  Video Feature & Media Coverage
    
    
      Successful Spintronics Terahertz Emission with Full Heusler Compounds
      
        Our study on full Heusler compound-based spintronic terahertz emitters (Co₂FeAl Full Heusler Compound Based Spintronic Terahertz Emitter, published in Advanced Optical Materials) was spotlighted by Advanced Science News (Wiley) with a dedicated feature video and highlighted by Physics of Magnetism, illustrating how high-amplitude THz emission is achieved across 0.2 to 4.0 THz bandwidths.
      
      
        
          
          Watch Feature on YouTube ↗
        
        
          Physics of Magnetism Post ↗
        
      
    
  

  
  
    
      December 2020  •  Journal Spotlight
    
    
      Applied Physics Reviews Highlights Review on Spin–Orbit Torques in 2D Materials
      
        The comprehensive status update review "Emergence of spin–orbit torques in 2D transition metal dichalcogenides: A status update" (Husain, Gupta et al.) was published in Applied Physics Reviews (AIP Publishing) and officially featured for its survey of 2D layered materials enabling efficient SOT manipulation in magnetic nanodevices.

  Open Positions at GHYAN Laboratory
  
    We welcome enthusiastic and self-motivated researchers to join our lab in the Department of Physics at IIT (ISM) Dhanbad.
  




  
  
    
      
        1. Postdoctoral Positions
        (IPDF / NPDF / Fellowships)
      
      Open
    

    
      We invite motivated postdoctoral candidates with background in experimental condensed matter physics, spintronics, magnetism, or computational micromagnetics/multiphysics.
    

    
      Fellowships: Open to candidates holding or applying for ANRF/SERB N-PDF, Institute Postdoctoral Fellowship (IPDF), CSIR, UGC, or other national fellowships.
      Form a Project: Prospective fellows are encouraged to contact the PI to jointly formulate and develop a competitive research project proposal.
    

    
      
        Contact PI to Form a Project →
      
    
  

  
  
    
      
        2. PhD Positions
        (Institute Funded & JRF)
      
      Open
    

    
      We welcome applications from prospective PhD candidates interested in exploring spin, orbital, and hybrid quantum phenomena in thin films and heterostructures.
    

    
      Funding Schemes: Positions are available through IIT (ISM) Institute Fellowships and external fellowships (CSIR-UGC JRF, DST-INSPIRE, or valid GATE/NET qualification).
      Application: Prospective candidates should email Dr. Rahul Gupta and formally apply via the IIT (ISM) Dhanbad PhD Admission Portal.
    

    
      
        Email PI →
      
      
        Admission Portal ↗

Central Research Facilities

title: Research
text:
The GHYAN lab explores the intersection of fundamental quantum physics and next-generation device applications, focusing on spin and orbital angular momentum in thin films, 2D heterostructures, and nanodevices.
  

  
    
      
      Research Areas
    
    
      
      Grants & Funding
    
    
      
      Collaborations
    
    
      
      Invited & Oral Talks
    
    
      
      Academic Visits
    
  







Research Areas


Core experimental thrust areas investigating quantum angular momentum, ultrafast dynamics, and device physics




Magnetism & Spintronics
We study the fundamental magnetic properties of novel quantum materials and how electron spin can be utilized for energy-efficient memory and logic devices. By understanding spin transport, spin-orbit torque (SOT), and spin dynamics, we aim to design next-generation magnetic RAM (SOT-MRAM) and spin-logic architectures that drastically reduce standby and switching power consumption.

  Key Publications
  
    
      
        Harnessing orbital Hall effect in spin-orbit torque MRAM ↗
      
      Nature Communications 16, 130 (2025)
    
    
      
        Strong In-Plane Magnetization and Spin Polarization in CFGT/Graphene Heterostructure Spin-Valve ↗
      
      ACS Nano 18 (7), 5240–5248 (2024)
    
    
      
        Emergence of spin–orbit torques in 2D transition metal dichalcogenides: A status update ↗
      
      Applied Physics Reviews 7, 041312 (2020)
    
  








Orbitronics
Beyond the spin degree of freedom, orbital angular momentum offers an exciting, energy-efficient dimension for information processing. We investigate orbital angular momentum-driven transport phenomena, including the orbital Hall effect (OHE) and orbital Rashba-Edelstein effect, in light metals (such as Ru, Cr, etc.) and transition metal oxides, unlocking pathways for high-efficiency torque generation without relying on heavy or scarce elements.

  Key Publications
  
    
      
        Identification of orbital pumping from spin pumping and rectification effects ↗
      
      Nano Letters 25 (36), 13462–13467 (2025)
    
    
      
        Itinerant orbital Hall effect mechanism leading to large negative orbital torques from light metal vanadium ↗
      
      arXiv:2508.16339 (2025)
    
    
      
        Nonreciprocity in magnon mediated charge-spin-orbital current interconversion ↗
      
      Nano Letters 25 (8), 3247–3252 (2025)
    
  








Terahertz Spin-Orbitronics
Exploring the generation, manipulation, and detection of terahertz (THz) radiation using ultrafast spin-orbitronic heterostructures. By exploiting inverse spin and orbital Hall effects, anomalous Hall phenomena, we develop ultra-broadband, low-cost spintronic THz emitters (STEs) for high-speed wireless communication, radar, and non-destructive spectroscopic imaging.

  Key Publications
  
        
      
        Terahertz emission from β-W/CoFe epitaxial spintronic emitters ↗
      
      arXiv:2401.10123 (2024) (accepted in Scientific Reports)
    
    
      
        Direct evidence of terahertz emission arising from anomalous Hall effect ↗
      
      Scientific Reports 13, 5988 (2023)
    
        
      
        Co2FeAl Full Heusler Compound Based Spintronic Terahertz Emitter ↗
      
      Advanced Optical Materials 9 (10), 2001987 (2021)
    
  








Quantum Sensing: Spin-Orbit/Orbital Torque and Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) Centers
We aim to utilize nitrogen-vacancy (NV) diamond center magnetometry and atomic-scale quantum sensors to non-invasively probe nanoscale spin configurations, stray magnetic fields, and spin currents with high spatial resolution and sensitivity. By integrating NV center quantum defects with magnetic heterostructures, 2D quantum materials, and spintronic devices, we investigate local spin-orbit torque switching, magnon dynamics, and topological spin textures (such as domain walls and skyrmions) from cryogenic to room temperatures.
